messages:
Ana V: Heads up — observed a persistent p99 spike on shared-pool-7 starting ~2332109600. p50 looks fine but p95/p99 doubled for ~30m. Pattern: tenant 'pixie' long-seq steady traffic => lots of quantized kernel paths.
Sam K: interesting. did kernel selector logs show switches?
Ana V: yes, selector.log shows repeated flips to `quant_int8_kernel_v2` under concurrency. When concurrency spikes the kernel picks quant path and latency climbs. excerpt: `selector: model=redwood-q-3b seq=1024 conc=12 chosen=quant_int8_kernel_v2 est_lat=42ms`
Jordan P: pinging profiling team. can you grab a CPU/GPU timeline and KV hit/miss rates for that window?
Lee Ops-bot: runbook check: for noisy-tenant alerts on shared pools, enable per-tenant sampling and stash profiles. created ticket RI-4578.
Maria S: I grabbed a quick flame with the runtime tracer. KV cache miss rate for pixie jumped from 8% -> 46% during the spike. KV churn looks correlated with the quantized kernel path (different memory layout causing more frequent KV invalidations).
Sam K: wow — so two factors: kernel selection change + KV thrash. any batching differences?
Ana V: yes, batching heuristics adjusted size down when quant path selected (we hit a conservative safety config). That reduced throughput and increased per-request overhead.
Jordan P: can you paste the commands you used to fetch traces?
Ana V: sure — reproducible snippet: 
```
runtime-admin profile --pool shared-pool-7 --since 2332109500 --until 2332110100 --kind gpu_timeline,kv_hist --out /tmp/pixie_spike.pb
runtimer-ctl logs --filter "tenant:pixie" --since 2332109500 > /tmp/pixie_kernel.log
```
Maria S: I also extracted a small sequence of requests and replayed them on a dev instance. Repro shows quantized kernel has higher tail variance for long seqs when KV miss rate >30%.
Sam K: hypothesis: quantized kernel has different KV slot eviction pattern; when combined with smaller batches the latency tail explodes. Proposal: 1) temporary per-tenant guardrail to avoid quantized kernels when avg_seq > 512 OR kv_miss_rate > 25%; 2) increase KV pinning budget for pixie; 3) gather perf counters to see memory access patterns.
Jordan P: +1 to guardrail as hotfix. Which config knob? I think `kernel_preference_policy` supports a list with conditional entries. We can add `prefer_fp16_for_long_seq` and gate by seq length.
Ana V: I drafted a conservative policy patch that prefers `fp16_kernel_v3` when avg_seq > 512 OR concurrent_requests > 8. Will file PR and test canary on shared-pool-7.
Maria S: practical mitigation for immediate relief: raised pixie KV pin budget from 64 -> 128 slots; that lowered KV miss rate to ~12% in my quick replay and p99 dropped ~30%.
Lee Ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled. deploy-bot: started canary of runtime v3.21.4 with kernel-pref patch on shared-pool-7 (canary: 5 nodes).
deploy-bot: canary health ok at 10m, no errors, latency trending down for pixie sample traffic.
Sam K: good sign. longer term we should: 1) add selector telemetry to summarize kernel flips per-tenant; 2) tighten batching heuristics so kernels with high tail get smaller concurrency budget instead of shrinking batch sizes globally; 3) consider tenant-level isolation thresholds (move heavy long-seq tenants to dedicated or reserved subpools).
Jordan P: + logging: include `kv_miss_rate` and `chosen_kernel` in per-request trace (low overhead counters) so we can alert on bad combos automatically.
Ana V: filed follow-ups: RI-4580 (telemetry), RI-4581 (batching heuristics refactor), RI-4582 (tenant isolation playbook). I'll attach replay artifacts to RI-4578.
Maria S: note for the perf team — when you profile, please include `sm_efficiency`, `l2_miss_rate`, and `warps_active` counters; quant kernels show different memory patterns.
Sam K: thanks all. short term: keep canary running 2h, then roll to rest of pool if stable. if we see recurrence we throttle pixie and offer them a Dedicated trial. :thumbsup:
Ana V: will monitor dashboards and post a summary in #incidents after the full rollout window. :thinking_face:
